author: reek
body: pci-enable-device brings a PCI device up, and until this test nothing had ever called it or its predecessor.

author: reek
body: So this reads the command register back off a real device rather than asserting the arithmetic. bit-or cmd 7 is not worth a test; what is worth a test is that the write reaches config space and the device keeps it.

author: reek
body: The second control is the untouched device. A config write that landed on the wrong device, or on all of them, would still show dev 0 going 3 to 7; dev 1 reading 3 afterwards is what says the address bits in pci-address select what they claim to select.

author: reek
body: The reads and the write are ordered by the let chain deliberately. They are typed pure -- Pci grounds Device.Port, so its own functions perform port I/O without publishing the row -- and a pure expression the compiler is free to reorder is exactly the wrong shape for a read-modify-read. Threading each step through a named binding is what fixes the order.
